style: Modern Japanese fantasy card-game one-shot. Warm, dry organic foley; no speech or music. Use metal or chimes only when explicitly requested.

sounds.prompt: One-shot game sound: thick matte cardstock sliding quickly off the top of a deck, close dry paper friction and a soft fingertip flick. Absolutely no metal, cymbal, bell, chime, glass, sparkle, or tonal ring.

One-shot variation: one heavy paper trading card pulled cleanly from a deck, short soft cardstock swish with a muted paper stop. Dry foley only; no metal, cymbal, bell, chime, glass, sparkle, or pitched tone.

One-shot entity entering play: a thick card placed firmly onto a felt-covered wooden table, ending in a warm low padded thump and tiny cloth movement. Physical and grounded; no magic sparkle, no metal, no chime.

One-shot entity entering play variation: quick cardstock movement followed by a confident soft landing on tatami and wood, a compact earthy low knock. No metal, no coins, no bell, no shimmer, no strange vocal texture.

One-shot fantasy spell release: a smooth gathered breath of air compresses into one clean soft energy pulse, then vanishes. Rounded and controlled, not hissy; absolutely no snake rattle, shaker, clicking, buzzing, metal, bell, or chime.

One-shot saber equip foley: a full-bodied cavalry saber and steel scabbard give one short low rattle against a leather belt, followed by a solid guarded settling clack. Weighty steel, not tinny, not a high-pitched ping, no music.

One-shot entity relocating from a narrow alley into an open garden: fast cloth and footsteps rush across a short wooden walkway, then land softly on soil and grass with a gentle open-air exhale. No paper, no page turn, no book, no bell, no magic sparkle.
One-shot martial attack movement: a very fast clean weaponless air swipe, sharp whoosh with a subtle bamboo snap, energetic but not cinematic, short and dry, no impact, no music.

One-shot martial attack movement variation matching a clean fast air swipe: lower soft cloth rush and a brief dry bamboo swish, natural and unpitched. No impact, no voice, no metallic tone, no whistle, no strange modulation.
One-shot light combat hit: a compact muted fist impact into padded cloth and leather, short dry body thump with a tiny air puff. No metal, cymbal, coin, bell, chime, glass, crack, or pitched ringing.

One-shot light combat hit variation: restrained palm strike into a padded training bag, soft dense thump and cloth compression. Foley only; no metal, cymbal, coin, bell, chime, glass, snap, or tonal sound.

One-shot heavy combat damage: one deep dense padded thud, like a heavy sandbag dropping onto tatami, with a short low body and no tail. No wood crack, no ceramic, no metal, no coins, no explosion, no ringing.
One-shot consequential leader damage sound: strong refined impact with deep taiko-like body, lacquered wood crack and very short dark resonance, dramatic but compact, no music.

One-shot cleansing water heal: a clear wave of fresh water washes gently across the listener, followed by one soft round droplet and a clean evaporating water mist. Restorative and pure; no bells, chimes, glass, crystals, metal, or music.

One-shot entity destruction: a low dry wooden break collapses immediately into soft earth and dust, compact and weighty with a muted finish. Absolutely no metal, coins, chain, glass, ceramic, clinking, bell, or sparkle.
One-shot mystical sacrifice: soft low pulse, paper talisman folding inward, then a dark airy dissolve with one subdued bell overtone, solemn and restrained, no voice, no music.

One-shot return-to-hand sound: a soft card lifts away from felt with a rounded reverse air pull and quiet cardstock flutter, gentle and low in brightness. No harsh high frequencies, no acid or caustic texture, no metal, whistle, chime, or snap.
One-shot resource gain: a small polished ceramic token placed down with a bright crystalline ping, clean modern Japanese fantasy interface sound, rewarding but subtle, no music.
One-shot resource spend: two quick muted ceramic token clicks descending slightly in pitch, tactile and restrained, clean game feedback, no cash-register sound, no music.
One-shot your-turn notification: one concise bamboo knock followed by a warm ceramic chime and tiny upward wind accent, calm focus, not an alarm, no music.
Short one-shot victory flourish for a modern Japanese fantasy card game: confident taiko accent, bright ceramic bells, and an elegant rising tonal resolution, celebratory but restrained, no voice.
Short one-shot defeat cue for a modern Japanese fantasy card game: subdued low drum, falling wooden and ceramic tones, gentle dark wind tail, dignified rather than tragic, no voice.

Short neutral match-end cue for spectators: one warm low taiko-style drum stroke followed by a quiet natural room decay and soft wind settling to silence. Clear finality but neither victory nor defeat; no melody, no metal, no bell, no chime, no voice.
